text:
maria (ml): Hey team — quick summary of the FP8/INT8/GPTQ/AWQ bakeoff across tasks (summarization, RAG QA, codegen).

maria (ml): TL;DR: FP8 maintains quality and gives best latency/cost for hosted; AWQ/INT8 variants give ~2-3x cost reduction but have task-specific regressions, notably in codegen EM and few-shot reasoning.

maria (ml): Raw numbers (median over 3 seeds):
- Summarization (ROUGE-L): FP8 +0.0, AWQ -0.7, GPTQ -0.4, INT8 -1.1
- RAG QA (exact match): FP8 +0.0, AWQ -1.9, GPTQ -0.8, INT8 -2.5
- Codegen (pass@1 EM simplified): FP8 +0.0, AWQ -3.2, GPTQ -1.4, INT8 -4.8
- Embeddings cosine drop: AWQ -0.2%, GPTQ -0.1%, INT8 -0.6%
- Latency (p95 tokens/s): FP8 1.0x baseline, AWQ 1.6x, GPTQ 1.4x, INT8 1.8x
- Cost per token: FP8 baseline, AWQ ~0.45x, GPTQ ~0.6x, INT8 ~0.4x

maria (ml): Observations: AWQ seems the fastest and cheapest but has a noticeable hit on codegen and multi-step reasoning. GPTQ is a safer middle-ground. INT8 (naive) is aggressive — biggest regressions on structured outputs.

kevin (infra): Interesting. are regressions correlated with sequence length or attention pattern? any kernel-level anomalies? :thinking_face:

maria (ml): We instrumented KV cache hit/miss and found larger deltas for long-context (>=1024) in AWQ/INT8. Also some attn scaling differences show up in unit tests for positional encodings — possibly quantization of rotary params.

sara (platform): For rollout decisions, we need concrete canary + fallback rules. Proposed approach: hosted = FP8 default, AWQ as optional low-cost variant behind canary; dedicated = allow GPTQ/INT8 for reserved pools with opt-in; private = recommend customer-run testing (no automatic switch).

james (product): Agree on conservative defaults. Can we put measurable thresholds for automatic fallback? e.g., quality drop >1.5% EM or p99 latency > target => rollback.

maria (ml): Proposed automated rules (draft):
```
rollout_policy: {
  canary_pct: 1.0,                    # start at 1% traffic
  evaluation_window: 60m,             # rolling 1 hour
  quality_metrics: ["rouge-l","exact_match","pass1_em"],
  quality_thresholds: {               # absolute drop vs control triggers fallback
    "rouge-l": 0.8,                  # percent points
    "exact_match": 1.5,              # percent points
    "pass1_em": 2.0                  # percent points
  },
  latency_thresholds: {               # absolute multipliers
    "p95_latency": 1.25              # if >25% worse than baseline -> rollback
  },
  fallback_order: ["fp8","gptq","full_precision"],
  max_canary_duration: 4h,
  escalation: "pager+slack-#eng-ml"
}
```

sara (platform): That looks good. small suggestions: initial canary 0.5% on hosted (so we see production noise), escalate to 5% over 3 steps if metrics stable. For Dedicated we can be more aggressive: 5% -> 25% -> 100% depending on SLOs.

kevin (infra): For routing: add a traffic router flag `route_by: ["quality","latency","cost"]` so customers can prefer minimal cost or max-quality. Also need fallbacks for model-unavailable: auto-route to pinned model version in same family.

maria (ml): Agreed. Also add per-customer QA sets (gold prompts) that run in canary window — helps catch domain-specific regressions (customer A saw -5% on codegen earlier).

rollout-bot: automated test results posted: canary run 1763700000-01:
- AWQ @1%: pass window 30m, rouge-l delta -0.6, pass1_em -2.9 -> FLAGGED for pass1_em > threshold
- GPTQ @1%: pass window 30m, all metrics within thresholds

james (product): Based on that, hosted should not auto-promote AWQ beyond 1% for general chat/code endpoints. Allowed promotion only for summarization/embeddings routes.

sara (platform): Action items:
- @maria: create per-task benchmark slices and add them to canary harness (ETA 2d)
- @kevin: implement `route_by` and fallback routing to pinned model (ETA 3d)
- @james: update product docs to reflect conservative defaults for hosted/dedicated/private (ETA 1w)
- @rollout-bot: include model family in canary emails

maria (ml): Also adding a short checklist for ops when promoting quant variants:
1) run customer-gold prompts (10x each)
2) check delta on pass1_em and exact_match
3) validate embeddings via cosine threshold
4) run p95 and p99 latency tests under synthetic load
5) if all good, promote 1% -> 5% -> 25% with 1h hold per step

kevin (infra): One more caveat: Dedicated GPUs with multi-tenant pools may see different perf. Add `pool_profile` in rollout metadata so the router can pick quant variant only on compatible pool types.

maria (ml): Noted. I'll upload the full bakeoff artifact (logs + eval slices + raw outputs) to the S3 bucket and link in the canary run. For now, holding AWQ on code endpoints and allowing AWQ for summarization/embeddings with our rollout_policy above.

sara (platform): Sounds good. If anyone objects, speak now otherwise I'll bake this into the default canary template and run the next scheduled canary tomorrow.

james (product): +1

kevin (infra): +1

maria (ml): Thanks — will follow up with the artifacts and a quick PR to the canary harness config.
